Q: Is there a better way to do this clunky function (maps, arrays, sets or none of them)? A:

You're right to be concerned about this. It is already repetitive, and as the number of types grows, it will only become more so.

My take would be to build this atop a function which accepts an object like this:

{
  buff:   ["gunslinger", "teamwork", "sharpness", "distraction", "trick", "undying", "badassery", "stability"],
  debuff: ["fire", "fear", "grappled", "infection", "prone", "limping", "dizziness", "slumber"]
}

and returns a new function which accepts your type and chooses the correct list by key, then randomly chooses one of its members. Let's call it makeRandChooser.

But that in turn would use a function which took an array of values and randomly chose one of those. Call it randMember.

And finally that one would depend on a function that given upper and lower bounds, chose a random integer between them. You already seem to have this, and you called it randNum.

Put together, it might look like this:

// Helpers
const randNum = (lower, upper) => lower + Math.floor(Math.random () * (upper - lower))
const randMember = (choices) => choices [randNum(0, choices.length)]
const makeRandChooser = (categories) => (type) => randMember (categories[type] || [])

// Our function
const randStatus = makeRandChooser({
  buff:   ["gunslinger", "teamwork", "sharpness", "distraction", "trick", "undying", "badassery", "stability",],
  debuff: ["fire", "fear", "grappled", "infection", "prone", "limping", "dizziness", "slumber",],
})

// Tests
console.log(Array.from({length: 5}, () => randStatus('buff')))
console.log(Array.from({length: 5}, () => randStatus('debuff'))) 
.as-console-wrapper {max-height: 100% !important; top: 0}

Now if you need another category, all you do is to add a new key and its associated array/

Q: CyberSource sandbox payments API returning SYSTEM_ERROR A:

First-party sandboxes going down is unfortunately common — you're blocked until they fix it, with no workaround.

If you have CyberSource's OpenAPI spec (or can export one from their docs), you can generate your own sandbox that you control:

npx fetchsandbox generate ./cybersource-openapi.yaml

FetchSandbox creates a stateful mock from any OpenAPI 3.x spec — CRUD works, state transitions work, and it runs locally or on our hosted platform. No dependency on the vendor's sandbox availability.

Won't replace CyberSource's sandbox for final integration testing, but it unblocks development when their environment is down.
